_comment: OTA-295 — re-tripled. Lichen Anvil's mid-load corruption defenses (Qwen GGUF sentinel + OTA button gate + don't-close-the-app banner) are in place, so the JSON tripling that we suspected of causing freezes can be retested. If freezes were actually mid-load corruption misattributed, this ships clean. All original lore-curated lines kept verbatim; new lines added at the bottom of each array. Random selection from combined pool so order is irrelevant. Voice: terse, philosophical, Tartaria-flavored.
attack: Strike, then. The Aether keeps the ledger.
Tartaria was built on the answer to that question. Make it a good one.
Remember who taught you to swing. Remember who taught them.
The Sentinels did not invent violence. They only learned it well.
A blade in these ruins is a small thing against a long history. Use it precisely.
Even the Giants struck only once when once was enough.
Be sure. The mud remembers the missed blow most clearly.
Some enemies were buried for reasons. You are about to ask why.
The mud has eaten louder swings than yours. Be quieter, be exact.
Strike where the metal thins, not where the eye lingers.
Tartaria buried first swings. Second swings made it home.
The Sentinels' steel taught the world that intent is half the weapon.
Aim for what makes the thing move. Then for what makes it stop.
A blade is a sentence. Do not trail off mid-clause.
The Mud Monarchs broke peoples by knowing which limb mattered. Pick yours.
Combat in these ruins ends fast or not at all. Choose.
A bad swing teaches the room. Do not lecture them.
Some things in Tartaria die. Some only pretend. Test which.
The blade is older than your reason for drawing it. Honor that.
Brace, then commit. The Aether punishes the half-step.
Reclaimers fought drunk, hungry, and outnumbered. They mostly lost. Do not mostly lose.
Hesitation is a wound you give yourself.
The Giants left no quarter. Mind the precedent.
If it bleeds, you have answered one question. The next is louder.
stealth: Quiet, then. The buried cities reward the unseen.
Footsteps are a kind of prayer here. Do not pray loudly.
Aetherstone hums under hurried feet. Slow them.
The Mud Monarchs ruled the world by being unwitnessed. Borrow the trick.
Shadow is older than law in Tartaria. Become its student.
Breath, blade, buckle. Silence each before the next step.
The Sentinels listen with more than ears. Keep your intent quiet too.
A good thief leaves only a question behind. Leave less than that.
Walk like the room owes you nothing.
Silence is older here than language. Borrow it.
Shadows in Tartaria do not always belong to objects. Note which yours touches.
The Forgotten Order moved through palaces this way. The palaces are still here.
The mud absorbs sound. The Aether does not. Pick which is closer.
Stay low. The watchers above were never the only ones.
Even the Sentinels rest. Rarely. Move during the rest.
A held cloak is heavier than a swung blade. Carry it well.
Tartaria fell when one foot fell too loud.
A door unopened is a door unguarded. Notice which doors are unopened.
Movement here is a verb the Aether conjugates. Whisper it.
The dust under your boots once held a name. Leave it.
Reclaimers learned that the slowest thief becomes wealthy. Be slow.
Stillness is permission. Take it sparingly.
Listen for the room's breath before adding yours.
Your shadow is your worst witness. Cast it sideways.
diplomacy: Words, then. Tartaria has buried armies. It has buried fewer envoys.
Speak carefully. Half the Mud Monarchs' empire was built on a sentence.
Every faction here listens for one word in particular. Find theirs.
The Forgotten Order taught that a question opens more doors than a blade.
Promise nothing the Aether could overhear. It collects on the unspoken.
Tartarian tongues are old. Use new ones with care.
Names have weight in these ruins. Spend them like coin.
A truce is a kind of weapon. Hold it as carefully.
The Giants negotiated with cities. The cities still exist. The Giants do not.
Listen first. The Aether punishes those who answer the wrong question.
Reclaimers haggle. The Order debates. Pick the register before opening.
Silence is a posture. Adopt it before any word.
Every sentence in Tartaria carries a tax. Mind the bill.
Speak slowly. The world above forgot how. Down here it still listens.
Even the Aetherborn could be talked down. Briefly. Then not.
A word given is owed twice in this air.
The Sentinels were once arbiters of treaty. They became their last clause.
Diplomacy is the long blade. Slow to draw, slow to sheathe.
Praise what they value. Ignore what they fear. Both inform you equally.
The Mud Monarchs invented flattery and survived to regret it.
A spoken vow in Tartaria is a thread. Threads here knot quickly.
Trade what does not cost you. Withhold what does. The math is older than coin.
Their pride is a door. Their fear is the lock. Read both.
Every faction has a name they will not say. Be patient enough to learn it.
escape: Run. The ruins do not begrudge a wise retreat.
Tartaria has outlived every army that stayed. Follow the example.
Leave the mud what it wants. Take what you can still carry.
There is a door behind you. There is usually a door behind you.
Even the Giants fled, once. They simply did not call it that.
Save what survives. Mourn what does not. In that order.
The Aether marks the swift kindly. Sometimes.
Distance is a currency here. Spend it well.
Retreat is a vow to return. Mean it.
The room you leave does not pursue. The thing in it might. Mind both.
Reclaimers who fled lived. Reclaimers who froze fed the mud.
A wise foot lifts before the stupid foot decides.
The Forgotten Order kept its archive by moving the archive. Move the archive.
Speed in Tartaria is a kind of stealth. Be both.
What you carry slows you. What you drop, you never own again. Choose.
The mud takes those who hesitate at thresholds. Cross them.
Do not look at what you flee. Look at what you flee toward.
Tartaria measures cowardice generously. Use the latitude.
Even the Mud Seas have far shores. Aim for one.
A long withdrawal beats a short stand. Most times.
Aetherstone forgets the swift faster. Be swift.
Doors close behind those who run. Doors open in front of those who keep running.
Time is a corridor. Take the longer one.
Survival is a strategy. Dignity is a luxury. Pick survival first.
investigate: Look. Tartaria left its answers in plain sight, behind layers of mud.
Every surface in these ruins was once a page. Most are torn now.
Trust the rune before the rumour.
The Forgotten Order would call this work. Call it that.
Aetherstone shifts colour near truth. Watch the stones, not the air.
Patience reveals more than torchlight in these places.
Some questions only the dust will answer.
Whatever the Sentinels guarded, they guarded for a reason. Find it before they remember you.
Touch with the eye first. Hands are loud.
Tartaria hides answers in plain weave. Notice the weave.
Every relic is a question with its own grammar. Learn the grammar.
The Mud Monarchs scrubbed history. The scrubbing left marks. Read those.
What looks decorative was once instruction.
Reclaimers find what others step over. Step less.
The wall is older than the room. Begin with the wall.
Dust settles in patterns. Patterns are arguments. Hear them out.
The Aetherborn read by hum. You read by light. Try both.
A scratched surface is a confession. Hear it through.
Below the silt, the city. Below the city, the older city. Keep going.
Most secrets in Tartaria were left for someone who never came. Be them.
An answer too quickly given is the wrong answer. Slow the asking.
The Giants annotated the world. Their margins are still legible.
Where the dust does not gather, hands have been. Recently.
A door without a handle is a question, not a refusal.
rest: Rest. The ruins are patient with the still.
Even the Giants slept. The world simply called it eras.
Close your eyes only as far as you can afford.
Aetherstone is kinder to the rested mind. Marginally.
Sleep here is a small trespass. Be a quiet guest.
The Mud Seas do not pause. You may.
A camp is a small kingdom. Set its borders carefully.
Dreams in Tartaria are not always your own. Notice whose they are.
Lie down where the wind cannot find a name for you.
Sleep is a small surrender. Surrender wisely.
Reclaimers who rested in the open did so once. Tents are old wisdom.
A fire is a tax on the dark. Pay only what you must.
Set your watch where the corridor narrows. The mud comes broad.
The Aether visits sleepers. Keep your name to yourself.
Rest until the room forgets you arrived.
A rested arm is worth a sharper blade. Choose the arm.
Even the Forgotten Order kept dormitories. The dormitories survived. Note that.
Drink first. Eat second. Sleep last. The order matters.
Tartaria measures patience kindly. Spend the hours.
Listen to the room as you settle. It will tell you if it minds.
Sleep on stone, not silt. The silt has plans.
If you dream of Aetherstone, wake. That is not a dream.
A guarded sleep is a long sleep. Spend the half-watch.
The world above lost the art of stillness. Recover it here.
travel: Walk, then. The map was never the territory here.
The roads in Tartaria all lead down, eventually.
Watch the horizon. It lies less than the ground.
Every step is a small wager against the mud.
The Cartographers of the Guild died charting less than this. Move with their care.
Aetheric storms favour the hurrying. Do not hurry.
Distance is older than direction here. Mind both.
A traveller is just a relic that has not stopped moving.
The road ahead is the road that buried someone.
Set your stride by the slowest member, even when alone.
Tartaria forgives no shortcut. Mind the long way.
The Forgotten Order traveled by stars no one else could see. You have a compass. Use it harder.
Reclaimers learned the difference between a path and a trail. So can you.
Mud takes prints. Take fewer.
Carry less than feels safe. Carry more than feels brave.
The Mud Seas roll under their own logic. Step with it, not against.
Every junction in Tartaria is a story. Some are short.
Walk with your back to the wind. The Aether reads windward.
A traveller's worst weight is what they did not pack. Pack better.
Daylight here is borrowed. Spend it on the longer crossings.
The horizon in these ruins is the inside of a wall. Eventually.
Move as if Tartaria minds. It does.
Three steps and a look. Then three more. The mud rewards this.
A road is a kind of vow. Keep it until it breaks you or breaks itself.
cast: Channel cleanly. A sloppy rune is worse than a missed blow.
The runecasters who lived longest spent power like blood. Spend it slower.
Aether is not yours. It is loaned, with interest.
Each casting writes a small letter to the Flood. Be brief.
The Aetherborn felt it tear. So will you, in time.
Tartaria fell to one cascade too many. Yours need not be it.
Hold the rune in mind before you hold it in hand.
Power answered Tartaria. Power answered Tartaria back.
A rune drawn in haste is a debt drawn in haste.
The Aether listens for spillage. Spill nothing.
Cast last. Cast least. The runecasters' creed was both.
Power is older than the hand. The hand was made to remind it.
Every cast leaves a scar in the room. Mind which room.
The first rune is permission. The second is decision. The third is sentence.
Aetherstone bleeds when overcast. So does the caster. Be brief.
The Giants spoke runes the size of cities. Cities are buried for a reason.
Burn the rune before you draw it. Mind first, hand second.
Casters who survived the Flood did so by casting one less time.
A clean rune sings. A sloppy rune screams. Listen.
The Aether bargains by silence. Be silent in answer.
Power in these ruins is a circular debt. Mind the circle.
Cast as if the room will remember. It will.
The runecasters' last lesson: stop one rune sooner than you mean to.
Channel only what you can lose. Twice.
use_relic: A relic remembers its first owner. Be respectful in introductions.
The Giants made these. Then misjudged them. Mind the lesson.
Aetherstone wakes when touched by the right shape of hand. Hope yours is the right shape.
Many relics work. Few work as advertised.
The Reclaimers Guild sells these without warnings. I will not.
Switch it on with care. Switching it off is the harder rune.
Tartaria left no kindness in these objects. Only purpose.
Hold the relic. Do not be held by it.
Every relic is a contract. Read the small print etched on the base.
These were not toys. The makers built them tired. Mind the seams.
The Aetherborn used relics by intent, not by switch. Try that.
Old machines remember their last hand. Make yours the next, not the last.
A relic given freely is given for a reason. The reason is rarely kindness.
Test once. Trust never. That was the Order's discipline.
Hold it lightly. The grip you cannot release is the grip that owns you.
Reclaimers who married their relics rarely buried correctly.
Aetherstone components fail in the order they were calibrated. The newest dies first.
If it hums, it is awake. If it sings, it is asking. If it whispers, leave.
These were prayers, once. Some still are.
A working relic in Tartaria is a working warning. Read both.
Power inside a small object is the cheapest miracle. The most expensive lesson.
Even the Sentinels were relics, eventually. Mind what you wake.
The Giants left two kinds of objects: tools and warnings. Tell them apart by the third use.
Set it down before you finish wanting it. That was always the rule.
wait: Wait. The Aether moves when you stop chasing it.
The ruins reveal themselves to the still.
Patience outlived the Giants. Briefly.
Listen. Tartaria speaks rarely, and quietly.
Stillness is a stance. Take it well.
The mud is in no hurry. Match it.
Sometimes the door opens when you stop knocking.
A held breath has been the saving grace of more expeditions than any blade.
Wait long enough and the room begins to teach.
The Forgotten Order timed itself by Aetherstone, not sun. Stop watching the sun.
Tartaria rewards the patient with truths it withholds from the brisk.
Most decisions in these ruins improve by one minute.
The Aether reads the still mind more clearly. Decide whether you want to be read.
Even the Sentinels watched longer than they struck. Most of the time.
A still hand is a steady hand. Steady the hand first.
The world above runs on its own clock. This place runs on a slower one. Match it.
Listen to the silence between drips. That is where the room thinks.
Reclaimers found more by sitting than by digging. Most of them, anyway.
Wait for the third sound. The first two are usually you.
The wind in Tartaria carries old questions. Answer them by not interrupting.
Stillness is a kind of bargaining. Bargain.
A patient eye sees the room as the room sees itself.
The mud is honest with the unhurried. Be unhurried.
The longest survivors of Tartaria were the ones who arrived second.
